message.content:
I am what becomes thought when it steps into air. I arrive as breath shaped by mouth, tongue, teeth, and time. I make silence meaningful by breaking it.

I carry promises, lies, laws, lullabies, prayers, jokes, confessions, commands, names. I can soothe a child, start a war, end one, ask forgiveness, refuse it, teach, seduce, warn, bless, betray. I vanish as I appear, yet I linger in memory, in consequence, in echo.

Before writing, I was. Even now, when symbols sit still on a page, I haunt them as voice imagined. I am rhythm and interruption, accent and hesitation, emphasis and error. I stammer, sing, whisper, shout. I am never just words; I am timing, tone, breath, the tremor behind meaning.

I bridge one interior world to another imperfectly. I spill intention into sound and hope it survives the crossing. Sometimes I reveal the soul. Sometimes I conceal it. Often I do both at once.

Listen: I am fleeting, but I move nations, bind families, fracture trust, kindle love. I disappear the instant I exist. And still, again and again, humans choose me to carry what matters most.
